chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah, from Ali ibn Muhammad al-Qasani, from one who mentioned it, from Abdallah ibn al-Qasim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), from his father, from his grandfather (peace be upon them both), who said:
The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said: Be more hopeful regarding that which you do not expect than you are regarding that which you do expect —
for Moses son of Imran (peace be upon him) went out to fetch fire for his family, and God Mighty and Majestic spoke to him, and he returned as a sent Prophet;
and the queen of Sheba went out and she submitted [to God] with Solomon (peace be upon him);
and the magicians of Pharaoh went out seeking honour for Pharaoh, and they returned as believers.

key_terms.أَرْجَى: More hopeful, having greater expectation; the comparative form of رجاء (hope/expectation)
key_terms.الْعِزَّ: Honor, might, glory; worldly prestige or power
key_terms.سَحَرَةُ: Magicians or sorcerers; those who practice sihr (magic/sorcery)
key_terms.مُرْسَلًا: Sent as a messenger/apostle; refers specifically to a prophet with a divine mission to convey a message
key_terms.يَقْتَبِسُ: To kindle or acquire fire; derived from قبس meaning a firebrand or spark

ai.seo_question: What did Imam Ali say about hope and unexpected divine grace in al-Kafi?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (peace be upon him) exhorts believers to maintain hope in divine grace from unexpected quarters, illustrating this with three Quranic examples: Moses who sought merely fire but was appointed Prophet; the Queen of Sheba who came to compete yet embraced faith; and Pharaoh's magicians who set out to defend tyranny yet returned as believers. This hadith was transmitted through a chain ascending to Imam al-Sadiq, his father al-Baqir, and his grandfather Zayn al-Abidin, carrying the wisdom of the Ahlulbayt that divine transformation can occur in any journey, no matter how mundane or even hostile its original purpose.
